title: Warmth slopes for within-month moth composition change were uncertain in four British samples in 1992-2015
abstract: We tested whether monthly warmth was linked to within-month change in moth catch composition. We compared early and late visits and subtracted a distance between alternating visits from the same trap-month. Both distances used a finite-catch correction. Four samples covered England and Scotland in 1992-2003 and 2004-2015, with 557 trap-months. Models controlled trap by month, year, rain and visit timing. Slopes were -0.06, +3.64, -0.70 and -0.70 distance units per C. All four corrected intervals included zero. Only a later English sensitivity model with linear time in place of year effects had an interval above zero. The strict later Scottish sample was too small to fit. The results do not establish a common warmth link or its absence. Few sites, selected visits, coarse weather and taxon-specific capture limit inference. Pooling nights also limits the finite-catch sampling assumption. No air pollution or extreme-event effect was tested. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and checks support reproduction from external inputs.

display.caption: Warmth slopes for early-late and alternating visit distances, and their paired difference. Bars adjust for four tests within each outcome. Every main excess-distance interval includes zero.

citations.reason: Adapt source-selection and retrieval code and reuse six source snapshots. Records overlap; the new test compares dates within months.
Adjacent-year composition study motivates the distance correction, but tests a different time scale.
